data.narrative:
Terrestrial Energy operates in the nuclear energy sector at the public stage, having raised $280M to date. The valuation universe comprises 8 comparable companies: 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private peers (Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, NuScale Power). However, the narrow peer set in nuclear energy presents a significant constraint on traditional valuation methodology.

The peer-median approach is not applicable here. The nuclear energy sector contains only 4 same-sector comparable companies total. Of these, none satisfy the requirement of at least 3 datapoints within the same stage or adjacent stage, nor do any cluster at similar valuation tiers. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial methodological error given the specialized capital requirements and technical risk profile unique to nuclear technology development. This scarcity of directly comparable public and private financings at comparable development stages undermines confidence in multiples-based approaches.

Without sufficient peer density to support triangulation, valuation requires reliance on alternative frameworks: discounted cash flow analysis contingent on commercialization timelines, comparable transaction multiples if available from M&A activity in the subsector, or venture capital method calibrated to the stage-appropriate return requirements. The $280M raised provides a floor reference point. Key uncertainties include regulatory pathway timelines, capital intensity to commercialization, and technology risk relative to competing modular reactor platforms. Additional private market transactions or public comparable IPO data would be necessary to establish a defensible valuation range.
